study_identification_part.si_4_title: Spectral normative modeling of brain structure

nm2_1_modeling_methods.detail: Hierarchical Bayesian Regression (HBR) was used as the normative modeling approach (direct method) within the SNM framework.
nm2_1_modeling_methods.supporting_text: "we focus on an exemplary instantiation using Hierarchical Bayesian Regression (HBR)"; "we utilize HBR as the normative approach used for the direct method"
nm2_1_modeling_methods.location: Mansour2025.pdf.md: 4.8 Normative Modeling Framework; Mansour2025.pdf.md: 4.8.2 Direct Method

nm2_2_response_variable.detail: High-resolution cortical thickness maps (vertex-wise) derived from T1-weighted structural MRI using FreeSurfer.
nm2_2_response_variable.supporting_text: "FreeSurfer processing of the T1-weighted (T1w) structural brain imaging data was used to extract high-resolution maps of cortical thickness."

nm2_3_explanatory_variables.detail: Covariates included age (modeled with a B-spline basis expansion), sex, and batch effects for harmonization across the three imaging cohorts.
nm2_3_explanatory_variables.supporting_text: "we consider the covariates of age and sex"; "Batch effects were included in the model to facilitate harmonization among the three imaging cohorts (development, young adult, and aging)."; "A B-spline basis expansion (cubic spline with three evenly spaced knots; df=5) was used to capture the non-linear effects of age. The fixed effect of sex is modeled by intercepts"
nm2_3_explanatory_variables.location: Mansour2025.pdf.md: 4.4 Normative Covariates; Mansour2025.pdf.md: 4.8.2 Direct Method
